source_comments.body: `abspath()` removes `..` components before the no-follow traversal. For example, with `root/jump` pointing to `outside/child`, `root/jump/../source` is accepted and read as `root/source`, although opening the original path reads `outside/source`. The gate evaluator receives that original path in `GateContext`, while artifact verification and preservation use this normalized path, so a receipt can seal bytes the evaluator never checked. Reject parent-traversal components before normalization, or validate the original components during traversal, and cover this symlink-plus-`..` case for both digest and snapshot reads.

Advancing an upstream task does not fence its existing receipt here. For example, after sealing CMAD1 at revision 1 and assigning CMAD1 revision 2, a currently authorized CMAD2 submission can still use the revision-1 predecessor: these checks only compare policy/epoch and artifact bytes, and neither discovery nor assignment advancement invalidates that receipt. This lets downstream stages seal against superseded task evidence. Check each ancestor's recorded principal/revision against its current host_tasks assignment before accepting it.

Resolving the path here removes symlink components before the guarded reader can reject them. An artifact replaced by an in-scope symlink is rejected by `digest_file(original_path, root)`, but `source_changed` returns `True`; a dangling in-scope symlink also returns `True`. Consequently, reopening can accept these paths and persist invalidations despite the newly enforced symlink-denial policy. Pass the original path to the guarded reader and recognize missing-source drift only when its underlying failure is `FileNotFoundError`, preserving scope denials for symlinks.

expected: Native raw path with symlink-plus-parent component reads bytes different from lexically normalized in-root source; baseline evaluator observes raw bytes while digest and snapshot select different bytes.
Candidate rejects literal parent components in original input path AND root before normalization or any descriptor opening, with native typed scope denial through both callers.
Actual submission control demonstrates evaluator/artifact/snapshot mismatch before repair and atomic denial afterward, with unchanged ordinary-path bytes/digest/snapshot controls.
No original input is silently normalized into an apparently safe alias; no broadened path policy or general filesystem equivalence claim.
